title: IAM blueprint modules for Private deployments (Terraform)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: provide a reusable, testable Terraform module set that bootstraps RBAC and least-privilege IAM artifacts for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The deliverable is a documented module registry entry and a migration playbook that operators can run against a customer VPC or on-prem control plane.

Scope:
- Terraform module: redwood/priv-iam (root wrapper) that composes smaller modules: roles, bindings, service_accounts, policy_templates, and health_checks.
- Support for AWS and GCP provider backends via provider-specific submodules (aws-roles, gcp-roles) while keeping the wrapper provider-agnostic for operator UX.
- Pattern library for tenant-scoped roles (operator-managed service roles, per-tenant user groups, and cross-account/organization assumed roles).
- Least-privilege role templates for common Redwood components (runtime nodes, control-plane agents, metrics-forwarder, backup service). Templates must be parameterized and additive to allow safe upgrades.
- Upgrade/migration plan: additive-only changes where possible, deprecation strategy, automated import and drift-detection helpers.
- Health checks: an IAM policy linter and a pre-apply plan checker that flags wide policies, unused permissions, and missing audit bindings.
- Test harness: Terratest integration suites + unit tests for Terraform templates, and a GitHub Actions pipeline that runs plan-and-diff in a sandbox account.

Design decisions & constraints:
- Keep default templates opinionated (least privilege) but expose escape hatches for customer-specific exceptions (explicit allowlist variables).
- Prefer provider-managed roles (AWS managed policies / GCP predefined roles) only when they reduce operational risk; otherwise create narrowly scoped custom roles.
- Avoid provider aliasing hacks in the root wrapper; require explicit provider blocks in the infra repo to reduce confusion across multiple accounts/regions.
- Terraform constraints: target >= 1.5, use of for_each/dynamic blocks and locals to minimize accidental resource recreation during upgrades.

Deliverables:
1) Module code in infra/modules/priv-iam with README, examples/ for single-tenant and multi-tenant deployments.
2) Migration playbook (markdown) documenting safe upgrade steps, import commands, and rollback guidance.
3) Health-check tool (go binary) that runs post-apply and emits a policy risk score.
4) Test matrix (GitHub Actions) + Terratest suites.
5) PR checklist and security signoff template for changes to role templates.

Operator UX flow (high level):
- Operator sets provider creds and runs terraform init/apply against example workspace.
- Module outputs role ARNs, service account emails, and a secure inventory CSV uploaded to S3/Cloud Storage.
- Health-check tool is run as part of CI and nightly checks (optionally as a Console health probe).

Success criteria:
- Module passes Terratest + plan checks in CI.
- Health-check detects at least two classes of policy risk (wildcards, over-broad resource ARNs) in synthetic test cases.
- Migration playbook validated in a staging customer cluster with zero privilege escalations during upgrade.
comments: 2026-01-26 - Spike: validated feasibility for a provider-agnostic wrapper. Found that keeping provider-specific role construction in submodules avoids huge conditional logic in root module. Notes: /docs/spikes/priv-iam-provider-spike.md

2026-02-02 - Design sync with Security: security team prefers custom, narrowly scoped roles for control-plane components. They requested an automated policy-lint step and an allowlist variable for legacy permissions.

2026-02-12 - Review with PM and infra: agreed on outputs contract (role ARNs, inventory) and to include a 'shadow-mode' apply that only adds tags/state for migration validation. PM asked for a one-page operator quickstart.
2026-02-20 - Security review request opened. Reference: Confluence page https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Priv+IAM+Blueprint (draft).

2026-03-01 - Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1347 - includes basic aws-roles and role templates for runtime nodes. Terratest scaffold added. CI currently failing on provider credentials in matrix jobs.
2026-03-05 - CI update: introducing sandbox account credentials via GH Secrets for plan-only runs. Added acceptance tests for a synthetic tenant which cover 12 role templates.

2026-03-09 - Findings from terratest: role name collisions observed when multiple tenants use the default naming scheme. Action: change to include tenant hash suffix and add terraform migration step to rename existing resources safely.
2026-03-10 - Next steps: finish GCP submodule, add health-check binary to module artifacts, and coordinate final security signoff. Assigned follow-ups to eng infra rotation.
acceptance_criteria: Module code in infra/modules/priv-iam with README and example workspaces
Terratest suites pass in CI for AWS and GCP plan-only runs
Health-check tool flags over-broad policies in test fixtures
Migration playbook validated in staging with no privilege expansion
Security team signoff recorded on Confluence
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Role explosion / combinatorial growth for multi-tenant templates. Mitigation: canonicalize templates and re-use parameterized roles; provide tenant scoping via bindings rather than duplicating roles.
Risk: Upgrades may cause drift or force-recreate of roles. Mitigation: additive changes only + import helpers and name-stability rules (tenant-hash suffix).
Risk: Operator confusion across cloud providers. Mitigation: clear examples for AWS/GCP and enforced provider explicitness in root module inputs.
Risk: Overly permissive policies slip through. Mitigation: policy-lint step in CI and a blocking health-check score threshold requiring security signoff.
